Subject: Follow-up: Data export controls / DPF evidence for Avalon PoC

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we start the procurement packet, our privacy team has a short set of follow-up clarifications related to cross-border transfers and the new US-EU Data Protection Framework (DPF). High level asks:

- Can you confirm which legal mechanism Redwood will rely on for EEA->US processing (DPF, SCCs, or both as fallback)?
- Technical evidence: encryption at rest and in transit, key management (who holds keys), and ability to restrict specific workloads to EU residents only (VPC/on-prem options).
- Data retention / logs: samples of retention policies and whether aggregated telemetry is exported to US accounts.
- Subprocessors: an up-to-date list and whether any subprocessors process inference requests outside EEA.

We have initial timelines for a PoC (June) and would appreciate an evidence pack we can include with our RFP. Can you send the technical pack and call out any items that will need contract language in the DPA annex?

Best,
Maggie
Maggie Turner
Senior Procurement Manager, Avalon Bio

Hi Maggie —

Thanks — attaching a focused evidence pack for the RFP (redwood-dpf-technical-evidence-2028-05.pdf) and our current subprocessor list. Summary answers up front:

1) Legal mechanism: Redwood will adopt the US-EU Data Protection Framework (DPF) where available for controller-to-processor transfers and will maintain SCCs (2021 standard clauses + UK addendum where required) as an operational fallback. We include language in our standard DPA annex that references DPF adherence plus SCCs for non-covered scenarios.

2) Key management: Customer data encryption-in-transit (TLS 1.3) and at-rest (AES-256). For hosted API we manage keys in KMS; for Dedicated/Private deployments we offer customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key via KMS/HSM integrations). We call out the option to restrict cryptographic material to EU regions in Private deployments.

3) EU-only processing: Private (VPC) deployments can be provisioned in an EEA region only; Dedicated pool commitments can be region-pinned. Hosted API is multi-region; we provide routing policies to prefer EU hosts but cannot guarantee exclusive EU processing for hosted multi-tenant endpoints without Private mode.

4) Logs & telemetry: Request-level metadata is retained per our retention matrix (attached). Aggregated telemetry (performance metrics) is pseudonymized and can be restricted by contract. Access to raw request logs is limited to named personnel and retained per retention schedule; we can provide longer retention for enterprise contracts by addendum.

5) Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors and locations. Any subprocessors processing inference payloads in non-EEA regions are flagged; we can offer contractual restrictions for the PoC.

Open items likely needing DPA annex language: 1) explicit DPF clause and fallback to SCCs; 2) customer-managed key options and key custody; 3) retention adjustments and audit access; 4) subprocessors and notice/objection windows.

We can schedule a short call Monday to walk through the pack and draft DPA annex language. Looping Neha (privacy) and Marissa (legal) to confirm technical phrasing.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Hi Maggie —

Quick clarifications from privacy so you can slot language into your RFP:

- DPF coverage: Redwood will self-certify to the DPF framework for processing governed under the Framework. Where customer contractual obligations require, we include SCCs as a fallback in the DPA annex. We will add explicit text stating the process for switching to SCCs if DPF coverage is no longer available for a given transfer path.

- Key custody: For Hosted API customers who require additional isolation, we offer a Dedicated deployment with customer-managed keys. For the PoC we can include a clause that any customer PII used in model tuning or evaluation will only be processed in EEA-hosted Dedicated instances if requested.

- Data minimization & pseudonymization: We recommend adding an optional technical control requiring request-level pseudonymization for exported datasets used for evaluation (we can provide a transformation script sample).

- Audit & evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary, annual penetration test summary, and cryptographic configuration export. Full SOC report can be shared under NDA.

I'll follow up with suggested DPA annex snippets for the points above by EOD.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data export controls / DPF evidence for Avalon PoC

Maggie —

Thanks for the clear asks. We attached a draft DPA annex (dpa-annex-draft-avalon.docx) that incorporates: DPF self-certification language, SCC fallback, customer key management options, retention SLAs and log access commitments, and a subprocessors notice/objection timeline (30 days). Specific notes:

- Subprocessor objections: we propose 30 days notice and mitigation plan; for mission-critical subprocessors we can offer a transition to Dedicated in-region hosting if objection is accepted.
- EU-only processing guarantee: provided via Private deployment (customer-managed infra) or via contractually constrained Dedicated pools. We will not claim EU-only processing for multi-tenant Hosted API.
- Incident handling: 72-hour notification for confirmed data breaches; support-level escalation matrix included.

Next steps: 1) confirm which evidence items Avalon needs in the RFP packet (SOC report under NDA? full penetration test?); 2) confirm whether PoC will require Dedicated/EU-hosted environments (we can provision a test Dedicated pool for June).

If that aligns, we can turn the DPA annex into a mark-up for your legal team and provide DocuSign-ready copy.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
